criteria.descriptor: Full marks: correctly defines B- (entity start), I- (continuation of same-type entity) and O (outside), states that every entity begins with B-, and describes a correct left-to-right decoding rule. Deduct for reversed B-/I- meaning, claiming the type-only scheme always works, or a decoding rule that mislabels boundaries.

Full marks: covers all four asked parts — tag definitions, the reason BIO is used (boundary marking), a concrete failure example for the type-only scheme, and the span-decoding procedure. Partial credit if the example or the decoding step is missing or only implied.

Full marks: explicitly ties the need for B- to separating adjacent same-type entities and justifies the failure example by showing why consecutive-run grouping collapses two spans into one. Lower if the failure is asserted without a mechanism or the example does not actually break the type-only scheme.
Full marks: uses correct terminology (span, token, tag prefix), and the worked example and decoding steps are concrete and easy to follow. Lower for vague, jargon-only, or disorganised explanations.

expected_answer_points: NER is a token-level sequence-labelling task, but the desired output is typed multi-token spans, so the label scheme must encode span boundaries recoverable from per-token labels
Defines BIO/IOB2 tags correctly: B-TYPE = first token of an entity, I-TYPE = continuation/inside token of an entity of that type, O = outside any entity
States that the B- prefix marks the start of a new entity, which is what lets two adjacent entities of the same type be separated
Gives a concrete example with two adjacent same-type entities where the type-only scheme wrongly merges them into one span while BIO keeps them distinct
Describes span decoding: B-X opens a span; subsequent I-X extends it; O, a new B-, or a type change closes it
Notes that model outputs can be malformed (e.g. an I-X not preceded by a matching B-X) and gives a sensible way to handle it
common_pitfalls: Picking an example with entities separated by O or of different types, which the type-only scheme handles fine, so it fails to demonstrate the actual weakness (adjacent same-type entities)
Reversing the tags — treating I- as the beginning of an entity and B- as the continuation
Answering about model architecture (CRF vs softmax head, transformers, BiLSTM) instead of the label-encoding question that was actually asked
Defining the tags but never describing how to decode a tag sequence back into entity spans
Claiming the type-only run-grouping scheme is always equivalent to BIO, missing that it cannot represent a boundary between two same-type entities
Ignoring that predicted tag sequences can be ill-formed (e.g. I-PER after O or after I-ORG) and giving no strategy to handle it
reference_answer:
NER is framed as sequence labelling: the model predicts one label per token, but the real output is a set of typed spans, so the label encoding has to let you recover span boundaries from per-token labels. In BIO (IOB2), every label is O (token is outside any entity) or a type prefixed by B- or I-: B-TYPE marks the first token of an entity of that type, and I-TYPE marks a continuation (inside) token of an entity already started with the same type. Crucially, every entity's first token is B-.

The B- prefix exists to mark boundaries between adjacent entities of the same type. The teammate's type-only scheme can't do this. Example: 'Alice Bob founded Acme' where 'Alice' and 'Bob' are two separate PER entities. Type-only tags them PER PER O ORG, so grouping consecutive same-type tokens merges them into one span 'Alice Bob'. BIO tags them B-PER B-PER O B-ORG, and the second B-PER signals a new entity, correctly yielding two people.

Decoding: scan left to right. A B-X opens a new span of type X; each following I-X extends the current span; an O, a B- (any type), or a differently-typed tag closes the current span. For robustness, handle malformed sequences — e.g. an I-X with no matching open span (or following a different type) — by treating it as a span start or dropping it, since raw softmax outputs aren't guaranteed to be well-formed.
